content:
maya: FYI seeing nvme metadata write_qdepth spike in eu-west4 at ~03:10 UTC, a few gpu attaches failed. looks correlated with janitor schedule shift :thinking_face:
ops-bot: ALERT nvme.meta_write_qdepth > 200 on gnode-93, gnode-37 (region=eu-west4)
jin: can you grab nvme stats + janitor logs from gnode-93?
maya: paste of /var/log/syslog tail from gnode-93:
```
[03:09:58] nvme0: meta_write_latency=21ms count=820
[03:10:05] nvme0: qdepth=212 reclaim-retries=44
[03:10:12] attach: nvme bind failed EIO
[03:10:18] janitor: starting metadata-deep-scrub job=8891
```
sam: that deep-scrub shouldn't have started until 02:00. scheduler drift?
lee: looked at leader election logs 1: leader moved to scrub-controller-5 (zone-b) due to a short restart; cron window calculation used local clock and got bumped. we lost the window guard.
anika: ops ask: can we pause the scrub for eu-west4 to reduce write pressure while we fix scheduling?
jin: proposed mitigations:
- suspend janitor deep-scrub cron for eu-west4 (graceful suspend)
- scale janitor-worker replicas in eu-west4 to 1 (limit concurrency)
- raise nvme metadata writeback throttle on hot nodes
- targeted evict/reclaim of hot ephemeral mounts on affected gnodes
maya: safest suspend command? I want no sudden job terminations.
jin: do both a cron suspend and graceful drain of running scrub tasks:
```
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob janitor-deep-scrub-eu-west4 -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n infra exec -it scrub-controller-5 -- /usr/local/bin/drain-scrub --graceful
kubectl -n infra scale deployment janitor-worker -l region=eu-west4 --replicas=1
```
sam: applied at 03:15 UTC. ops-bot recorded action.
ops-bot: ACTION pause-scrub eu-west4 by sam at 03:15 UTC
maya: meta qdepth dropped on gnode-93 from 212 -> 48 in 70s, attach backlog cleared. test jobs attaching now.
lee: created PR 4581: leader-affinity pin + lease health-check to avoid cron drift. added metric scrub.start_time_drift.
anika: any risk of metadata inconsistency from pausing? ops wants assurance for customers.
jin: low risk. deep-scrub checks, not mutations. we will run a controlled catch-up scrub at 04:30 UTC with concurrency=1 and pre-checks.
maya: please log estimated savings: avoided emergency GPU reprovisioning and potential cross-zone migrations. put number in incident tracker.
sam: collecting nvme metrics + attach logs 02:45-03:30 UTC and will drop into #postmortems later.
lee: TODOs:
- merge PR 4581 (lee)
- schedule catch-up scrub 04:30 UTC concurrency=1 (sam)
- monitor nvme.meta_write_qdepth for 6h and escalate if >100 (maya)
- add runbook note for pausing deep-scrub during GPU attach pressure (jin)
maya: thanks all, will watch for any recurrences :eyes:
ops-bot: NOTE collect_logs job scheduled by sam
